verbs.title: Read the grid
verbs.description: Read a building's grid: every grid line's id (gx0, gx1, … along x; gy0, gy1, … along y) and its position in metres in the building's own frame, plus the structural system, the material, the number of girders and the building's rotation in degrees. Opens a fresh copy of the building; takes about 10 to 40 seconds. Changes nothing.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Hospital" or "HospitalGarage".

verbs.title: Try shifting a grid line
verbs.description: Shift one grid line, and every later line on the same axis, by a distance in metres (positive = towards higher positions). Only the bay just before that line changes width; the rest of the building travels with it. The app makes the change, checks it (overlaps, beam spans against their limit, doors and windows against their walls) and returns its report: what changed, each check before and after, and what was not checked. If the change adds new problems the app undoes it and returns stopped_by_gate with the reason. Opens a fresh copy each time; nothing is saved.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, as in bim_lines.

inputs.name: line
inputs.description: The grid line to shift, e.g. "gx6".

inputs.name: move
inputs.description: The distance in metres, e.g. 1.824. Negative moves towards lower positions.

verbs.title: Count elements
verbs.description: Open a building in the Viewer and count its elements, the same answer the Viewer's Find panel gives for "Find element count by discipline" (or by storey). Returns the total and the count per group, plus the Viewer's own log line for the same answer. Opens a fresh headless copy of the Viewer on the CPU; takes about 20 to 90 seconds. Changes and saves nothing.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex" or "Clinic". An unknown name is an error.

inputs.name: by
inputs.description: What to count by: "discipline" (the default, e.g. ARC, MEP) or "storey" (floor level).

verbs.title: List clashes between two disciplines
verbs.description: Open a building in the Viewer and list the clashes between two disciplines, the same answer the Viewer's Find panel gives for "Find clashes between A and B": how many element boxes overlap at the rule's tolerance (in metres), how many of those are true clashes after the shape tests, and the first 20 rows with the overlap in metres. A pair with no clash rule is an error, not zero. Opens a fresh headless copy of the Viewer on the CPU; takes about 20 to 120 seconds. Changes and saves nothing.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Clinic". An unknown name is an error.

inputs.name: discA
inputs.description: First discipline code, e.g. "ARC" (architecture), "STR", "MEP".

inputs.name: discB
inputs.description: Second discipline code, e.g. "MEP". Order does not matter.

returns.shape: viewer_verbs JSON as viewer.counts, plus cols, rowsTotal, rows

verbs.title: Film path visibility
verbs.description: For a Viewer database that holds drawn services, report per film-camera band how many drawn lines and markers fall inside the film camera's view. Opens a headless copy of the Viewer on the CPU. Reads only: no bake, no GPU, nothing written. A database with no drawn services, or a path no sample of which lies on a band, is inconclusive, not zero.

inputs.name: db
inputs.description: Path to the Viewer database (.db) to judge.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Optional override file with the cinema_path bands to judge instead of the database's own.

returns.shape: film_path_vis --json {verdict SEES|BLIND|INCONCLUSIVE, per, totalLines, totalMarkers, log}

verbs.title: Widen a bay to a target width
verbs.description: Composed verb: read the grid, compute how far the line "to" must move so the bay from "from" to "to" has the target width (in metres), and try that shift, with the same checks and the same stop as modeller.try_shift. Nothing is saved.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name.

inputs.name: from
inputs.description: The grid line at the start of the bay.

inputs.name: to
inputs.description: The grid line at the end of the bay; this line and every later one on its axis moves.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: The bay width wanted, in metres.

returns.shape: the envelopes of its lines, in answer.lines; the last is modeller.try_shift's

verbs.title: Describe an object kind
verbs.description: Reflection. Given a kind (and optionally one record), return what the model's own dictionary says about it: each property (name, type, mandatory, updateable, key, list values, min and max), the child tabs below it, and the generic methods that are legal for it (read, update, attach, history). Reads only dictionary rows; no data row is opened. An unknown kind is an error naming it. Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: Optional. A record's UU; the answer then also names how its child tabs link to it.

verbs.title: Read an object
verbs.description: Read one record of a registered kind by its UU key, with the rows of its single-row child tabs (for an element, its transform). Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: The record's UU key (for an element, its IFC guid).

verbs.title: History of an object
verbs.description: The change-log rows legacy iDempiere would have written for one record, derived from the op-log of edits made through the object engine (column, old value, new value, event). Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: The record's UU key (for an element, its IFC guid).

verbs.title: Change one property of an object
verbs.description: Change one property of a record of a registered kind. The dictionary decides whether it may: the property must exist and be updateable, a list value must be on its list, a number must be a number, a mandatory property may not be emptied. A refusal says which rule. The change is written as an op to the op-log, not into the model file.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: The record's UU key (for an element, its IFC guid).

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: The property to change, as describe lists it, e.g. "element_name".

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The new value, as text.

verbs.title: Attach a file or note to an object
verbs.description: Attach a file (or a text note) to a record of a registered kind, the way the ERP window's Attachment button does: one attachment row per record, keyed by the record's UU. Written as an op to the op-log, not into the model file. A kind whose key is neither an _ID nor a _UU column cannot have attachments.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: The record's UU key (for an element, its IFC guid).

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: Path of the file to attach.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: A text note to attach, when no file is given.
